title: Question Type and Productivity: Delilah (11) and Bryanna (13)
summary: This webinar explores how different interviewing approaches affect the quantity and quality of information obtained from children. Through case examples, the presenters discuss the impact of open-ended prompts, potential investigator bias, and strategies for obtaining detailed narratives while maintaining a neutral interviewing stance.

title: Case Review: 13 year old Renee
summary: This webinar examines a case involving a 13-year-old who later recanted previous allegations of sexual abuse. The discussion focuses on common reasons children recant, how family dynamics and concerns about disrupting relationships can influence disclosures, and effective interviewing strategies for exploring prior statements without pressuring the child. Viewers will learn how forensic interviewers evaluate competing explanations for disclosure and recantation.

title: Case Review: 11 year old Matthew
summary: This webinar examines a case involving an 11-year-old boy who disclosed repeated sexual abuse. The presenters discuss unique challenges that may arise when interviewing male victims, including embarrassment, shame, reluctance to discuss abuse, and strategies for helping children provide detailed narratives in a supportive environment.

title: Case Review: 9 year old Faith
summary: This webinar reviews a case involving allegations of problematic sexual behavior between siblings and explores the challenges of interviewing children when caregivers disagree about what occurred. The presenters discuss credibility assessment, family responses to disclosures, and factors that may increase the likelihood of recantation or inconsistent reporting.

title: Case Review: 12 year old Lesly
summary: This webinar reviews a case involving repeated allegations of abuse and explores how caregiver responses can influence disclosure patterns. The discussion focuses on family support, disbelief, blame, and the role these factors play in children’s willingness to maintain or withdraw allegations over time.

title: Case Review: 14 year old Deavyn
summary: This webinar examines one of the lab’s early remote forensic interviews and discusses the benefits and challenges of conducting child interviews through video technology. The presenters review interviewing techniques, rapport building in virtual settings, and considerations for maintaining interview quality when in-person interviews are not possible.

title: Question Type and Productivity: Bryanna (13)
summary: This training-focused webinar examines forensic interviewing methods and the relationship between question types and the amount of information children provide. Using a real interview as an example, the presenters analyze open-ended questioning, narrative development, and techniques that encourage detailed and reliable responses.

title: The First Jane Doe in the Epstein case: S.G. (14)
summary: This webinar examines the disclosure history of the first known victim in the Jeffrey Epstein investigation and explores how child sexual abuse cases can be affected by delayed disclosure, reluctance, embarrassment, and inconsistent reporting. Through a review of police interviews, disclosure patterns, and investigative decisions, the presenters discuss common barriers to reporting, the impact of trauma on memory and disclosure, and the importance of supportive interviewing techniques when working with adolescent victims. The case highlights broader challenges that investigators encounter in sexual abuse and trafficking cases involving youth.

title: Recantation: Azul (13)
summary: This webinar focuses on a teenager who disclosed abuse to friends through social media before later recanting. The discussion highlights best practices for interviewing youth who have made multiple disclosures, documenting prior reports, and understanding how family reactions may influence a child’s willingness to maintain or withdraw allegations.

title: "Stuck in the same cycle everyday" Ashley (14)
summary: This webinar explores the challenges of interviewing adolescents who report repeated abuse occurring over extended periods of time. The presenters discuss how repeated experiences are often remembered as generalized patterns rather than distinct events, making it difficult for youth to describe individual incidents. The webinar examines the concepts of script memory and episodic memory, demonstrates strategies for eliciting detailed narratives, and highlights supportive interviewing techniques for children who are reluctant to discuss traumatic experiences.

title: "I’d rather go to jail than getting beat up by my dad" Kaden (15)
summary: We will be reviewing an interview Jordan conducted with 15-year-old Kaden. Kaden disclosed that his father was physically abusing him by punching him in the head. He also reported that he believed his father drugged him and his girlfriend and sexually assaulted Kaden’s girlfriend while Kaden was blacked out and incapacitated. When Kaden spoke to the CSW, he also reported that his father would threaten him sexually. Going into the forensic interview, Jordan anticipated Kaden might be reluctant to disclose the threats of sexual abuse because previous reports stated that Kaden couldn’t remember if any sexual abuse occurred.

title: "I can tell it was bleeding cause I like tasted blood" Ellie (9)
summary: We will be reviewing an interview I conducted with 9-year-old Ellie. Ellie disclosed to a school counselor that her mother hits her in her mouth and eye with an open hand. She stated the most recent incident happened the night before because she didn’t go to sleep. It was also reported by school officials that mother does not treat Ellie and her older brother the same. Mother punishes Ellie by not allowing her to participate in school activities, and does not provide Ellie with the same resources as her older brother. Going into the forensic interview, we thought Ellie might be reluctant to disclose because when she spoke to the CSW after her initial disclosure, she began to minimize the abuse.

title: "They keep on asking questions even though I tell them everything that’s the truth" Kaylee (11)
summary: We will be reviewing an interview Jordan conducted with 11-year-old Kaylee. Kaylee disclosed that she was self-harming because her brother and mother argue a lot at home. She reported that her brother gets violent and punches holes in the wall. Kaylee also disclosed a previous suicide attempt, so going into the forensic interview, Jordan knew that she might have to conduct a suicide assessment. During the interview, Kaylee got very upset and combative with Jordan for having to be interviewed by so many professionals about the same allegations. So Jordan had to explain the reasons why she was asked to speak with Kaylee.

title: "Everyone’s giving me different words for it" Claire (17)
summary: We will be reviewing an interview Jordan conducted with 17-year-old Claire. Claire disclosed that her father had been forcing her to have sex with him for two years. She reported that it happens every other night while the rest of their family is sleeping. During Jordan’s interview with Claire, she explained that the details of the different incidents were the same, so Jordan had to use creative techniques to get at multiple episodes.

title: "All I ever feel is guilt, and it’s exhausting" Josie (15)
summary: We will be reviewing an interview I conducted with 15-year-old Josie. Josie disclosed that her stepfather had been sexually abusing her since she was four years old. When Josie was interviewed by the police and social workers, she reported having a hard time remembering details of the abuse because she tried to forget it. During my interview with Josie, she talked a lot about self-blame and being an active participant in the abuse, which led me to change my questioning techniques.

title: "Gave me the ick" Back to Basics: Ruth (11)
summary: We will be reviewing an interview Jordan conducted with 11-year-old Ruth. Ruth disclosed that her stepfather was touching her inappropriately under the ruse of tickling. She also reported that he would take pictures of her in the shower. When Ruth was interviewed by her social worker, she denied these allegations, but then subsequently re-disclosed to the police. Going into the forensic interview, Jordan anticipated that she might be reluctant to disclose.

title: "My dad said it was not my dad, it was a person I was dreaming" Morgan (9)
summary: We will be reviewing an interview Chrissy conducted in 2017 with 9-year-old Morgan. Morgan disclosed that her father would wake her up to do “sexy stuff.” She reported that he would touch her butt with his front part, and “white stuff” came out. Prior to the interview, it was discovered that the mother and father had reunited. When Chrissy interviewed Morgan, she recanted her allegations, stating that it was just a dream and that she had gotten caught watching a sexy movie.
